terms.meaning: The oldest and simplest society: small, nomadic groups who hunt and gather wild food.
A society that lives by rearing herds of cattle.
A society that lives by cultivating large areas of land, using animals to plough.
A society that depends on industries using science and technology.
Dividing work according to workers' skills.

items.name: Size of a hunting group
items.formula: Never more than 40-50 people, in small scattered groups.
items.example: They used stone axes, spears and daggers.

items.name: Wealth and rule in hunting society
items.formula: No idea of wealth: they share everything.
items.example: No rulers and ruled, since there are no political institutions; family ties bind them.

items.name: Size of a cattle-rearing society
items.formula: Hundreds to thousands of people: the Bhaktiyari community has about 5000 to 1,50,000.
items.example: Found today in parts of Africa and Central Asia.

items.name: Where cattle-rearing societies live
items.formula: Grasslands, hills and deserts not fit for farming.
items.example: The person with the most cattle is the richest and leads.

items.name: The Farming Revolution
items.formula: Began with the plough around 3000 B.C.E.; animals pulling it raised food output more.
items.example: People settled in one place and villages formed.

items.name: Why new skills grew in farming society
items.formula: More food meant not everyone had to farm all day.
items.example: So people took up other work.

items.name: What changed industrial society
items.formula: The steam engine, internal combustion engine, electricity and nuclear energy.
items.example: People migrate to cities, so cities grow.

items.name: The four kinds as stages
items.formula: Hunting, then cattle-rearing, then farming, then industrial.
items.example: They can also be seen as stages of human evolution.

mistakes.text: Hunting groups are tiny (40-50); cattle-rearing societies are much bigger (hundreds to thousands).
Villages began with farming, not with hunting or cattle-rearing, which kept people moving.
In cattle-rearing society wealth is counted in cattle; the hunting society has no idea of wealth at all.
